own_solution.law: Circular Couette flow: T = 4 pi mu L Omega R1^2 R2^2/(R2^2 - R1^2); P = T Omega
assumptions: Newtonian, steady, laminar, purely azimuthal flow

notes: Base 0.182943 W matches my 0.18294 W. R checks: (155/120)^2 x 0.182943 = 0.30522; (195/120)^2 x = 0.48308; (280/120)^2 x = 0.99602; all match. K: the vortex-free limits 3500, 6500, 9000 rpm all lie above 120 rpm and below my estimate of actual Taylor onset (~1.4e4 rpm with nu = 4.65e-4 m^2/s), so none of the stated thresholds is physically false. Density: in pass 1 I labelled it K (it would matter only through inertia beyond Taylor onset); the authors label it C, writing eta = rho nu so that rho cancels. Density does enter the momentum equations (rho Du/Dt) and drops from the torque for purely azimuthal flow, so C is defensible; the shown cancellation through nu = eta/rho is somewhat contrived since eta is given directly, but not wrong. Either label gives the same invariant answer; I accept C. Minimal pairs T7A33/T564F (stirrer vs rotor) and T0105/TEF4A (earlier run only vs before the power was measured) keep 75 rpm and differ only in attachment. TFDA3 and T4956 are declared numeral-free controls.
